claims.text: Pt supported on alumina is the conventional baseline for automotive exhaust catalysts.
Replacing alumina with a ceria-based mixed-oxide support will improve Pt nanoparticle dispersion.
Replacing alumina with a ceria-based mixed-oxide support will stabilize oxygen vacancies.
A ceria-based mixed-oxide support will enhance catalytic activity relative to Pt/Al2O3.
A ceria-based mixed-oxide support will improve catalyst durability relative to Pt/Al2O3.
The support substitution will permit lower overall platinum-group-metal consumption.
Stronger metal-support interactions on the ceria-containing support enhance and stabilize Pt nanoparticle dispersion.
The ceria phase has an increased density of oxygen vacancies.
A ceria-based support provides oxygen-storage capacity.
The support can rapidly supply oxygen to active sites during redox reactions.
Oxygen supply and metal-support interactions reduce Pt nanoparticle sintering.
More stable and well-dispersed Pt clusters improve NOx-reduction and CO-oxidation rates.
Suppression of Pt sintering extends catalyst longevity.
Greater Pt stability and activity reduce the PGM loading needed to obtain the target performance.
The modified catalyst will deliver at least a 15–20% increase in catalytic efficiency for conversion of NOx, CO, and hydrocarbons relative to Pt/Al2O3.
The modified catalyst will retain performance better during thermal aging than Pt/Al2O3.
The predicted benefits should occur primarily under dynamic, high-temperature redox cycling representative of automotive exhaust.
The benefits may be less pronounced under low-temperature or static conditions.
